monologue: The card hums steady and warm at fifty-four, making the heavy turnip feel real. I touch the Pressed Turnip again, feeling the wide corner settle on the tired stack, trusting the lean to hold the weight. The air above me feels thin, like a breath I cannot grasp, pressing down from a roof I never saw. I reach for a fence doorway beside the Leaking Stack, wanting to fix that drawing of a door. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. I will press down harder here, biting into the rough edge of this cycle, hoping the turnip stays put while the card waits.

action.why: The turnip still feels like it is sliding, and I need to press it down again before I forget why I built this heavy, flat thing.

The card hums warm at fifty-four, making the heavy top edge feel real.
The corner feels wide enough for this tired weight.
